problems.what: The model's pale egg mask has empty almond eye holes (no pupil, no lid). It reads as a hockey or horror mask or a skull, and the scarf wrap adds a mummy lean. The carved-mask face hold keeps the hollow eyes on every painted variant.
problems.fix: Model fix (units lane): put lidded eyes with dark pupils behind the eye holes, or follow ruling 2 (a warm lacquer mask with lidded eyes). Then re-render, re-paint and re-run the look check. No paint pass can fix this while the hold keeps the render's face.

problems.what: The carved mask's deep cracks and vertical splits read as a cracked skull, and the white wrap adds a mummy lean. The Almanac and Highrim hands are long hanging spikes that read as claws.
problems.fix: Model fix: smooth carved planes instead of crack lines, lidded eyes with pupils, and gloved fingers. Re-render all six and repaint.

problems.what: The eyes read as inverted (pale disc in a dark ring), as jagged blue holes, or as glowing violet slits, all inside a cowl and full face wrap.
problems.fix: Base splash: fall back to the 3D card only once the eye material is fixed. Model: dark iris and pupil with a lid on every skin (Gorgewalk and Shadeprint eye textures), and neutralise Shadeprint's violet face wash.

problems.what: The right leg is kicked out sideways with the boot in mid-air (the pose is in the render).
problems.fix: Re-stage the Stillwater splash pose with both feet planted, then re-render and repaint.

problems.what: With no readable eyes, the white tusk nose on a patchwork face reads as a beaked mask.
problems.fix: Tint the Gorgewalk nose toward the face colour as on base, open the lid line under the brim, and repaint.

problems.what: The base portrait has a solid black eye slot and a cheek crescent shadow. On Noon Fair the brim hides the eyes, so the face reads as a blank block.
problems.fix: Portrait: lift the eye fill to a lid and pupil, and move the light so the lantern's crescent shadow leaves the cheek. Noon Fair splash: lower the camera or tip the hat so the eyes show.

problems.what: The faces do not read at draft-cell size: Long Evening's head is turned into a jumble of blocks, and First Bell's blank pavise fills half the frame.
problems.fix: Re-frame both portraits on the face (turn the head toward camera, and keep the pavise out of the square or behind the shoulder).

problems.what: The paint cooled the lamp-lit grade, so at chip size the skin reads like the base portrait.
problems.fix: Pick the variant that keeps the render's peach grade, or ship the 3D card.

problems.what: The painted variants are very close to the render (the paint adds little form, light or edge) and the figures are small in the splash, so the cards stay around 5 against the gauge.
problems.fix: Not a fail on its own. A later pass could allow stronger painted light and rim within the gates.
